c.tagline: Colonial capital high in the Andes, ringed by volcanoes.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are legally required to run the meter ('taxímetro') within the city; agree on a fixed fare in advance for airport trips or if the driver claims the meter is broken.

emergency.note: 911 (ECU 911) is Ecuador's unified national emergency line for police, fire, and medical services.

hood_landmark.Centro Histórico (Old Town): Plaza Grande (Plaza de la Independencia), Quito

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the Old Town & La Mariscal; take a taxi up El Panecillo; caution at night

hood_desc: Quito's backpacker and nightlife hub centered on Plaza Foch, packed with hostels, bars, and tour agencies; best for budget travelers and anyone wanting restaurants and nightlife within walking distance.

One of the largest and best-preserved colonial centers in the Americas, with cobblestone streets, churches, and grand plazas; ideal for culture lovers and first-timers, though it quiets down after dark.
A leafy, artsy enclave of galleries, independent cafes, and co-working spaces favored by young locals and creatives; suits digital nomads and foodies wanting a more residential, less touristy base.

Quito's modern business and financial district anchored by its namesake park, with high-rises, malls, and international chain hotels; good for business travelers and families wanting green space and extra safety.

An affluent valley suburb east of the city with a warmer microclimate, upscale restaurants, and easy access to the airport; suits families, longer stays, and travelers preferring a quieter, car-friendly base.

water.note: Aging pipes mean tap water can pick up contaminants; stick to bottled water.

transit.pay: Metro, Trolebús, Ecovía, and Metrobús-Q use an integrated contactless card (tap-in at turnstiles); cash is not accepted on the Metro. Regular city buses are typically paid in cash directly to the driver or fare collector.
transit.hours: Metro and BRT corridors generally run about 5:00/6:00 AM to 10:00/11:00 PM; there is no late-night rail service, so taxis or rideshare apps are used after hours.
transit.note: Quito's Metro Line 1 opened in December 2023, running roughly north-south beneath the city and complementing the older Trolebús/Ecovía trolleybus-BRT network.

train: Tren Ecuador heritage tourist trains departing Quito's Chimbacalle Station

transit.m: Aeroservicios airport bus to Río Coca terminal (~1 hr)

tip.r: A 10% service charge is often already added to restaurant bills; an additional small tip is appreciated but not obligatory. Taxi drivers are generally not tipped.
